parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Calculate the number of people living in rural areas in Madagascar in 2017.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Suggest two reasons why most people living in rural areas in Madagascar do not think
they will benefit from the development of sustainable tourism.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
As many as 300 000 tourists visit Madagascar each year.
Suggest three services that are needed by tourists.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text: Suggest two environmental problems that can be caused by large numbers of tourists.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Many tourists visit Madagascar to see the wildlife.
The photograph shows two lemurs. Lemurs are an endemic species in Madagascar.
Madagascar has 101 different species of lemur. Each species is adapted to a particular
habitat.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
A recent survey of Madagascar found that 42 species of lemur are at risk of extinction.
Calculate the percentage of lemur species that are not at risk of extinction.
______ %

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Define the term habitat.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
The habitat of many species of lemur has been reduced in recent years by deforestation.
Explain why deforestation occurs in some less economically developed countries
(LEDCs).

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text: Explain how soil changes after trees have been removed.

parts.label: (v)
parts.text:
Lemurs eat fruits, flowers and small insects.
Explain why lemurs can be classified as both a primary and a secondary consumer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
An area of mountainous rainforest covering 32 000 hectares has been set up as a wildlife
reserve to protect 12 different species of lemur. Some tourists visit the wildlife reserve after a
long journey over a rough track. There is a small visitor centre. If tourists stay overnight they
have to sleep in a tent and bring their own food.
The following activities also take place in the reserve:
• plant and animal populations are surveyed by scientists
• trees are replanted by local people
• methods of sustainable farming are taught to local people
• fuel-efficient cooking stoves are promoted.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Explain why surveys of plant and animal populations need to be done regularly.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Describe three different methods of sustainable farming.

2 (a) The drawing shows a disused chromite mine near the port of Toamasina.
The disused chromite mine was reopened in 2009.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Identify the type of mine shown in the drawing.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest two benefits of mining in this way.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
The chromite is being mined from igneous rock.
Explain how igneous rock is formed.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
The ore is processed at the mine to increase the concentration of chromite in the crushed
ore. The crushed ore is taken to the port of Toamasina for export.
Suggest one reason why the ore is processed at the mine.

parts.label: (v)
parts.text:
A mining company has a permit to explore and then mine an area of 2000 km .
Describe the environmental impacts of starting a new mine.

parts.label: (vi)
parts.text: Describe two economic impacts of mining.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Chromite is exported to other countries. Most chromite is used in the manufacture of stainless
steel.
In 2010 the world price of chromite reached 3000 USD per tonne. By 2012 the price had
fallen to 2000 USD per tonne.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Calculate the percentage decrease in the world price of chromite per tonne from 2010 to
2012.
______%

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest two reasons why the world price of chromite decreased.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Describe ways chromite can be used sustainably.

parts.text: Suggest why there is a high risk of toxic chemicals being washed out of the mining waste.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Some toxic chemicals can bioaccumulate in the environment.
Describe the process of bioaccumulation.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
There is a lake near the chromite mine.
A local fisherman said,
I used to catch lots of large fish.
I only catch a few large fish now, mainly I catch small fish.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest why there are only a few large fish to catch.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Describe possible changes in the food chain that could explain why local fishermen
mainly catch small fish.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Do you think fishing in this lake is a sustainable activity? Explain your point of view.
